object.title: Strong-product variation of Graham's pebbling conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be connected graphs, let $G\boxtimes H$ denote their strong product, and let $\pi(G)$ denote the pebbling number of a graph. The notation $|G|$ and $|H|$ denotes the numbers of vertices of $G$ and $H$, respectively.

**Strong-product pebbling conjecture.**
For any connected graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
\pi(G\boxtimes H)\leq \max\left\{\frac{1}{2}\pi(G)\pi(H),\ |G||H|\right\}+2.
$$

This is proposed as a variation of Graham's conjecture for strong products. The paper gives motivating bounds and an example showing that a simpler factor-$\frac12$ bound does not hold, while this sharper variation remains unresolved in the source.
object.source_name: John Asplund, Glenn Hurlbert and Franklin Kenter, “Pebbling on Graph Products and other Binary Graph Constructions”, arXiv:1801.07808 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.07808

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

object.title: The vertex-distinguishing total coloring bound
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with no isolated edges, and let $\chi_{r\text{-vsdt}}(G)$ denote its $r$-strongly vertex-distinguishing total chromatic number.

**Vertex-distinguishing total coloring conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{r\text{-vsdt}}(G)\le n+\lceil\log_{2}n\rceil+1
$$
\nand equality holds if $n=2^{k}-2$.

This conjecture proposes a general upper bound based on the number of vertices; the equality condition is motivated by the known values for complete graphs. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.

object.title: Erdős–Hajnal three-color triangle conjecture
object.statement: Let the edges of the complete graph on vertex set $[n]$ be colored with three colors I, II, and III. For a triangle with vertices $a<b<c$, consider the pattern in which $\{a,b\}$ has color I, $\{b,c\}$ has color II, and $\{a,c\}$ has color III. **Erdős–Hajnal's conjecture.** The number of triangles having this color pattern is at most $g_3(n)$. This conjecture is relevant because, for $k=3$, Erdős and Hajnal proved that it would imply their first growth-threshold conjecture. The source does not state a resolution of this three-color triangle bound.

object.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2019).

object.title: Singer graceful-graph conjecture for finite-field graph decompositions
object.statement: Let $[m]_q=(q^m-1)/(q-1)$ denote the $q$-analog of $m$. A graph is **Singer-graceful** when it satisfies the graceful-labeling condition associated with the Singer difference set. For integers $v$ and $i$ with $1\leq i\leq [v-2]_q$, let $\Gamma$ be a regular graph of order $[v-1]_q$ and degree $qi$. **Singer graceful-graph conjecture.** The graph $\Gamma$ is Singer-graceful, and consequently there exists a cyclic $2$-$(v,\Gamma,i)$ design over $\mathbb{F}_q$. This is presented as a specialization of the preceding difference-set conjecture; it would produce an infinite family of non-trivial graph decompositions over finite fields, and the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Marco Buratti, Anamari Nakic and Alfred Wassermann, “Graph decompositions in projective geometries”, arXiv:1907.03194 (2020).
object.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

object.title: Jackson's Tutte-cycle conjecture for 2-connected claw-free graphs
object.statement:
A graph is **claw-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,3}$. A graph is **2-connected** if it is connected and remains connected after deleting any one vertex. A **Tutte cycle** is a cycle $C$ such that every component of $G-V(C)$ has at most three neighbours on $C$.

**Jackson's conjecture.** Every $2$-connected claw-free graph has a Tutte cycle.

This is presented as an equivalent formulation of Thomassen's open conjecture on Hamilton cycles in 4-connected line graphs. The equivalence is obtained using the closure technique, but the conjecture itself remains unresolved.
object.source_name: Adam Kabela, Zdeněk Ryjáček and Petr Vrána, “Equivalent formulation of Thomassen's conjecture using Tutte paths in claw-free graphs”, arXiv:1907.08029 (2025).
object.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2019). “Conjecture remains open, even though partial results and numerous equivalent formulations of this problem are known (see survey ).”

object.title: Existence of a topological spanning tree-like subcontinuum in the tangle compactification
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\Lambda G$ be its tangle compactification. A **TST** of $\Lambda G$ is a spanning standard subspace of $\Lambda G$ that is also a TST-like subcontinuum. **Existence conjecture.** If $G$ is any graph, then $\Lambda G$ admits a TST.

This asks whether every graph's tangle compactification contains a spanning continuum with the prescribed separation-order structure. The supplied passage gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

object.title: The bounded vertex-deletion growth conjecture for Ramsey numbers
object.statement:
For graphs $H$ and $H'$ obtained from $H$ by removing a single vertex, let $r(H)$ and $r(H')$ denote their two-color Ramsey numbers.

**Vertex-deletion Ramsey conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c$ such that

$$
r(H)\leq c\cdot r(H').
$$

The conjecture is presented as a way to remove the logarithmic factor in the concentration result for random-graph Ramsey numbers; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

object.title: Aharoni–Berger's common independent-set partition conjecture
object.statement:
Let $M_1=(S,\mathcal{I}_1)$ and $M_2=(S,\mathcal{I}_2)$ be loopless matroids. Write $\rchi(M_i)$ for the coloring number of $M_i$, namely the least number of independent sets into which $S$ can be partitioned. **Aharoni–Berger conjecture.** The ground set $S$ can be partitioned into

$$
\max\{\rchi(M_1),\rchi(M_2)\}+1
$$

common independent sets. This would give the best possible upper bound, as described in the source, for covering the ground set by common independent sets; the supplied text does not state a resolution.
object.source_name: Kristóf Bérczi, Tamás Schwarcz and Yutaro Yamaguchi, “List colouring of two matroids through reduction to partition matroids”, arXiv:1911.10485 (2020).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2019).

object.title: Erdős et al.'s conjecture on almost-monochromatic congruent triples
object.statement:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a three-point set, let $s_0\in S$, and call a copy of $(S,s_0)$ **almost-monochromatic** if the points corresponding to $S\setminus\{s_0\}$ have one colour while the point corresponding to $s_0$ has a different colour.

**Erdős et al.'s conjecture.** There is a non-monochromatic colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$ that contains no almost-monochromatic copy congruent to $(S,s_0)$ if and only if $S$ is collinear and $s_0$ is not an extreme point of $S$.

This conjecture characterizes the three-point configurations for which a non-monochromatic colouring can avoid almost-monochromatic congruent copies. The source attributes it to Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus; no resolution is given.

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

object.title: The predicted piecewise-quadratic formula for the Ramsey-Tur\e1n density
object.statement:
Let $f\colon(0,1]\longrightarrow\mathds R$ be the Ramsey\e1Tur\e1n density function. For $k\ge2$, define

$$
f_k(\alpha)=k(k-1)-2k(3k-4)\alpha+(3k-4)(3k-1)\alpha^2.
$$

**Ramsey\e1Tur\e1n density formula.** The function $f$ is given by

$$
f(\alpha)=\begin{cases}
\alpha,&\alpha\le\frac13,\\
f_k(\alpha),&\frac{k}{3k-1}\le\alpha<\frac{k-1}{3k-4}\text{ for some }k\ge2,\\
\frac12,&\frac12\le\alpha\le1.
\end{cases}
$$

This is the precise prediction for the density function that would follow from the preceding extremal conjecture. Thus its status is tied to the still-open range $\alpha\in(\frac13,\frac38)$, while the portions corresponding to the established cases are known.
object.source_name: Tomasz Łuczak, Joanna Polcyn and Christian Reiher, “On the Ramsey-Turán density of triangles”, arXiv:2001.11474 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.11474

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

object.title: Jackson's Hamiltonian cycle conjecture for 2-connected bipartite graphs
object.statement:
Let $n$, $m$, and $b4$ be integers with $n > b4$. Let $\mathcal G(n,m,b4)$ denote the set of bipartite graphs with parts of sizes $n$ and $m$ in which every vertex in the part of size $n$ has degree at least $b4$. **Jackson's conjecture.** If a graph $G \in \mathcal G(n,m,b4)$ is $2$-connected and satisfies

$$
m\leq \left\lfloor \frac{2(n-\alpha)}{b4-1-\alpha} \right\rfloor (b4-2) + 1,
$$

where $\alpha = 1$ if $b4$ is even and $\alpha = 0$ if $b4$ is odd, then $G$ contains a cycle of length at least $2\min(n,b4)$. This conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Alexandr Kostochka, Mikhail Lavrov, Ruth Luo and Dara Zirlin, “Longest cycles in 3-connected hypergraphs and bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2004.08291 (2020).
object.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.08291

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

object.title: Finite-group gain-graphic well-quasi-order conjecture
object.statement: Let $H$ be a finite group. A **gain-graphic matroid** is a frame matroid obtained from a graph with edge gains in $H$, and a class is **well-quasi-ordered** when it has neither an infinite strict descending sequence nor an infinite antichain under the relevant minor relation. **Finite-group gain-graphic well-quasi-order conjecture.** The class of $H$-gain graphic matroids is well-quasi-ordered. If true, every minor-closed class of $H$-gain-graphic matroids would have at most finitely many excluded minors that are themselves $H$-gain-graphic. The source says this is widely believed and expected to be approachable, at least for abelian $H$, while the corresponding assertion fails for infinite groups.
object.source_name: Daryl Funk, Dillon Mayhew and Mike Newman, “Defining bicircular matroids in monadic logic”, arXiv:2005.04526 (2021).
object.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2020).

object.title: The Erdős–Discrepancy majority-coloring conjecture
object.statement:
Let $A_{s,k}=\{s,2s,\ldots,ks\}$ be a homogeneous arithmetic progression, and let an $h$-majority coloring be a red-blue coloring $c$ satisfying

$$
c(s)\sum_{j=1}^{k}c(js)\leqslant h.
$$

**Majority-coloring conjecture.** There exists a constant $h$ and a red-blue coloring of $\mathbb N$ which is $h$-majority on every homogeneous arithmetic progression $A_{s,k}$. This is a relaxed version of the Erdős Discrepancy Problem; the source does not give a resolution.
object.source_name: Bartłomiej Bosek and Jarosław Grytczuk, “Reflections on the Erdős Discrepancy Problem”, arXiv:2005.14283 (2020).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

object.title: Edge-size conjecture for graceful zillion graphs
object.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a zillion graph with $\omega$ odd cycles and $\mu$ even cycles, and let $|E(\Gamma)|$ denote its number of edges. **Edge-size conjecture.** There exist a quadratic polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and a linear polynomial $g\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $\Gamma$ is graceful whenever

$$
|E(\Gamma)|\geq f(\omega)+g(\mu).
$$

Kotzig's lower bound, as adapted in the source, shows that a zillion graph with $\omega$ odd cycles must satisfy a quadratic lower bound in its number of edges for gracefulness. The proposed conjecture gives a quadratic contribution from odd cycles and a linear contribution from even cycles, and remains open.
object.source_name: A. C. Burgess, P. Danziger and T. Traetta, “On the Oberwolfach problem for single-flip 2-factors via graceful labelings”, arXiv:2010.07231 (2020).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

object.title: Odd-Hadwiger conjecture for signed graphs
object.statement:
Let $(G,-)$ be a signed graph whose underlying graph is $G$, with every edge negative, and let $(K_{k+1},-)$ denote the complete graph on $k+1$ vertices with every edge negative. A signed graph $(H,\pi)$ is a **minor** of $(G,\sigma)$ if it is obtained by deleting vertices or edges, contracting positive edges, and switching. **Odd-Hadwiger conjecture.** If $(G,-)$ has no $(K_{k+1},-)$-minor, then

$$
\chi_c(G,+)\leq k.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the Hadwiger conjecture and generalizes Catlin's result, whose case $k=3$ is stated in the source. Its status is not resolved in the supplied material.
object.source_name: Reza Naserasr, Zhouningxin Wang and Xuding Zhu, “Circular chromatic number of signed graphs”, arXiv:2010.07525 (2020).
object.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07525

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2020). “Kardos and Narboni refuted this conjecture by constructing a non-4-colorable signed planar graph.”

object.title: Barát–Gyárfás–Sárközy conjecture for rainbow matchings in multigraphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a properly edge-colored multigraph with $2n-t_n$ colors and exactly $n$ edges of each color, where

$$
t_n=\begin{cases}0&\text{if }n\text{ is even},\\1&\text{if }n\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Barát–Gyárfás–Sárközy conjecture.** Then $G$ has a rainbow matching using $n$ colors.

The conjecture concerns the number of colors needed when every color class has exactly $n$ edges. The source cites best-known partial results, but does not state a resolution of the conjecture.
object.source_name: Debsoumya Chakraborti and Po-Shen Loh, “Large rainbow matchings in edge-colored graphs”, arXiv:2011.04650 (2026).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.04650

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2020). “Gao, Ramadurai, Wanless, and Wormald refuted Conjecture in by constructing an example where $\D$ is linear in terms of the number of colors used.”

object.title: The $(k)$-total coloring conjecture
object.statement:
Let $k\geq2$ be a fixed positive integer and let $G$ be a graph. **$(k)$-total coloring conjecture.**

$$
\chi”(G)\leq\Delta(G)+k.
$$

This is presented as a weaker version of the total coloring conjecture obtained by relaxing the upper bound. The case $k=2$ is the original total coloring conjecture, while larger $k$ give weaker assertions; the supplied text does not indicate a resolution of this general formulation.

object.title: Karskiński–Łuczak–Thomason 1-2-3 Conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph without isolated edges. An edge-coloring is **neighbor-sum-distinguishing** if any two neighboring vertices have different sums of the colors on their incident edges. **1-2-3 Conjecture.** Every graph $G$ without isolated edges admits a neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-coloring with the colors $\{1,2,3\}$. The conjecture asks whether three colors always suffice; the best known general upper bound is five colors, so the conjecture remains open.

object.title: Odd Hadwiger's conjecture
object.statement:
Let $(G,-)$ be the signed graph obtained from a graph $G$ by assigning a negative sign to every edge, and let $(K_t,-)$ be the all-negative signed complete graph. A signed graph minor is obtained by vertex deletion, edge deletion, contraction of positive edges, and switching at vertices. **Odd Hadwiger's conjecture.** If $(G,-)$ is $(K_t,-)$-minor-free, then

$$
\chi(G)\leq t-1.
$$

This is a strengthening of Hadwiger's conjecture introduced independently by Gerards and Seymour. The cases $t=3$ and $t=4$ are known, the case $t=5$ implies the four-color theorem, and all remaining cases are open according to the source.

object.title: Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan positive and negative square-energy conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple undirected graph with $n$ vertices, adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$, and positive and negative square energies

$$
s^+(G):=\sum_{\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i^2,\qquad s^-(G):=\sum_{\lambda_i<0}\lambda_i^2.
$$

**Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan conjecture.** Every connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfies

$$
\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}\ge n-1.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is proved using a framework based on doubly nonnegative matrix relaxations of positive semidefinite matrix Hadamard squares.
object.source_name: Yinchen Liu, Quanyu Tang and Shengtong Zhang, “The positive and negative square-energy conjecture”, arXiv:2607.18031 (2026).
object.references:
